about.label: The Designer
about.sub: An independent designer making clothes that look impossible — until you see them in person.

story.label: The Story
story.headline: Clothes that belong in a film you can't quite place.
story.p1: Women's clothes usually pick a lane: invisible, or trying too hard. Kaylah skipped the choice and built three dresses instead.
story.p2: Each one shares the same bones — a corset bodice, a sweetheart neckline, a pleated skirt — and tells a different story. Pink satin that feels like a Barbie dream. Ice blue that belongs on a catwalk in Paris. Polka dots that make you think of Marilyn Monroe on a rooftop.
story.p3: The name says it all. Pretty Absurd is fashion that's deliberately, joyfully out of place. Clothes that make people stare — not because they're strange, but because they're exactly right in all the wrong ways.

philosophy.label: The Philosophy
philosophy.quote: "Pretty Absurd is built on one idea: clothes should make you feel like the most interesting person in the room. Not the most tasteful. The most interesting."
philosophy.body: Feminine or serious. Playful or polished. Women hear that split constantly. Kaylah ignored it. The corset boning is serious. The polka dots are playful. Both, at once, on purpose.

process.label: The Process
process.headline_2: The chaos happens when you wear it, not when we make it.
process.step1_text: Every dress starts with the bones. The corset boning defines the silhouette before a single piece of satin is cut.
process.step2_text: The fabric is the personality of the piece. Satin catches the light differently. Polka dots change the conversation before you say a word.
process.step3_text: The ruffle at the sweetheart neckline. The lacing at the back. The invisible zip at the side.

cta_strip.text: Three dresses. Pre-ordering opens 25 July — Collection drops 25 July 2026.

brandWorld.label: Brand World
brandWorld.intro: Polka dots on subways. Grass in living rooms. A perfectly pressed dress in an entirely wrong place. This is the world the clothes come from.

manifesto.one: The dress that doesn't match the setting. The fabric too beautiful for the occasion. The silhouette that stops the room. Nobody plans to remember an outfit. Pretty Absurd makes sure they do.
manifesto.two: The references are everywhere: Marilyn Monroe on a subway grate, Barbie in a dream house that isn't quite right, a Vogue editorial shot in a place Vogue would never go. Pretty Absurd borrows from all of it — and puts it in a corset.
manifesto.three: This isn't fashion that wants to disappear into the wardrobe. It wants to be worn, looked at, and worn again.

letter.title: from Kaylah…
letter.p1: she arrived late, unbothered, and slightly too much for the room… which is, of course, the entire point. this issue is a small love letter to the dress — the one you don't need but will absolutely buy — and to everyone who understands that being pretty is optional, but being absurd is a lifestyle.
letter.p2: we made her by hand, in small numbers, on purpose. what follows is how she came to be… and how you take her home.

editorial.quote: she doesn't ask for the room. she simply refuses to leave it.
